items.title: Wallace Davenport Interview, 1995-11-14
items.q: I played there once, with Professor Victor's band.

ctx.x: Now, this, in around 1933, 32, 33, is when I went there. But, uh. What kind of place was it? Just a dance hall? It wasn't anything polished. It was just like a dive. But that was the only place that we had to go to have entertainment. I mean, if you didn't go to one of those places, you'd go to a house where they used to have those fish fries. Like, did you ever hear that number, Saturday night, fish fries? Sure. Sure, Louie Jugg. Well, who was playing at the
Pigpen? Did you play at the Pigpen? I played there once, with Professor Victor's band. But

that's where the old, I mean, that's where the professional musicians played. Now what I mean by professional musicians, the guys who were playing for the big money, a dollar and a half a night. Right. Were these dances they played for? Yeah, dances, yeah. Dances. Sometimes I think about the money that they paid us, and the money that the musicians were, and they were glad to make that money. Some of them used to play for nothing.
